- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by +1–3% to align with true mean reversion.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment >0.5 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction of 1–3% per sentiment reversal day.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day forecasts — if recent 10-day average is >10% above forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment-neutral periods (0.0), model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply smoothing filter to avoid overreaction to minor price noise.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- Model often underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) true values when sentiment is positive — apply 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
